review: Our guide knew a taco stand that isn't on any map. I still think about it.
Perfect snow and a guide who knew every run. My legs gave up on day three, but I'd still go back.
New York, LA and San Francisco in nine days, and it never felt rushed. The free afternoons were my favorite part.
The barrel tasting at Beringer was a real treat. I just wish we'd had a bit more time at each winery.
Good wine, good food, good people. Ben made every tasting fun, even for someone who knows nothing about wine.
On our second night the whole sky turned green. I cried a little. Worth every cold minute.
I didn't know the sky had that many stars. Bring a jacket, trust me.
Beautiful water and lazy beach days. The boat ride was a bit bumpy for my stomach, but the sunset in Key West made up for it.
Easy trails, huge mountains and lakes so blue they look fake. Steve knew the name of every bird we saw.
Aspen Highlands was amazing. Beaver Creek was busy the day we went, but our guide still found us quiet slopes.
Every park looked like another planet. Falling asleep in a tent at Joshua Tree was my favorite night of the year.
Surfing, skating and jumping out of a plane, all in one trip. Loved it, but you really need to be fit. I needed a vacation after this vacation.
Warm drinks by day, green skies by night. Kate woke us up the moment the lights came out, so nobody missed a thing.
Nine strangers, five days, one very patient elk. Best week of my year.
Fresh snow every morning and hot chocolate every afternoon. Jennifer got me down my first really steep run without falling once.
Antelope Canyon glows like the inside of a lantern. I took 400 photos and none of them do it justice.
Bagels in New York, sunshine in LA and cable cars in San Francisco. Miyah made every day feel easy.
Five days of sunshine, hills full of grapes and amazing cheese plates. I didn't want to come home.
I came for the wine and stayed for the people. Our little group still has a group chat.
Leo pointed out planets I'd only seen in books. Lying on a blanket in Death Valley at midnight is something I'll never forget.
The skydive over San Diego was the scariest and best minute of my life. Two weeks of nonstop fun.
Three cities, zero stress. Kate knew a great place to eat in every one of them.
I'm not a hiker and I still loved it. The trails were easy, the views were huge and the snacks never ran out.
The water at Sombrero Beach is so clear you can see your toes. Seven days of pure summer.
Jasper took my breath away. Kate made sure the slowest walker in our group (me) never felt left behind.
Loved New York and San Francisco. LA felt a little rushed, but I'd book this trip again in a heartbeat.
Horseshoe Bend at sunset, then a sky full of shooting stars. I made a wish on every single one.
The lights only showed up on one of our three nights. That night was magic, but it was a lot of waiting around in the cold.
Miyah knew every hidden beach in the Keys. Watching the sunset in Key West with my new friends was the perfect ending.
Fresh air, cold lakes and the best sleep I've had in years. Perfect for a first hiking trip.
Steep runs and deep snow all day, then hot chocolate by the fire. The best ski trip I've ever taken.
The parks were stunning, especially Zion. Camping for most of the trip was a lot for me, but the views made it worth it.
Rafting the Kern River was the best part. Some days were really long, so pack snacks.
I saw the Milky Way with my own eyes for the first time. Steve brought a telescope and hot tea. Ten out of ten.
Clos Pegase looks like an art museum, and the wine is even better. Miyah planned every stop perfectly.
Yellowknife is cold, really cold, but standing under the dancing lights made me forget all about it.
Way too much for me. I was worn out by day three and the schedule never slowed down. I spent the second week wishing I'd booked the Wine Taster.
Leo had a story for every tree and mountain, and Glacier National Park was the best day of the trip.
Sun, boats and beaches for a whole week. Jennifer found us the quietest spot on every island.
Beaver Creek on a sunny morning is a dream. Ben pushed me to try harder runs and I'm so glad he did.
Standing at the edge of the Grand Canyon made me feel tiny in the best way. Aarav's campfire stories were a bonus.
I stood up on a surfboard for the first time at Point Dume and climbed in Yosemite the next week. I feel unstoppable.
Short trip, huge memories. The sky turned green and pink and I just stood there with my mouth open.
We saw elk, a bear (from very far away) and the bluest lakes I've ever seen.
Great runs and a fun group. Four days went by so fast, I wish it was a little longer.
Zion, Antelope Canyon, the Grand Canyon and Joshua Tree in one trip. Kate made camping feel easy, even for a city kid like me.
San Francisco was my favorite. There's a lot of walking, so bring good shoes.
The skate park day was so much fun. It's a tiring trip, but the guides kept everyone safe and smiling.
No city lights, no phone signal, just a billion stars. I didn't miss my phone once.
Raymond was the perfect last stop. Great wine, great views, and nobody had to drive. What more could you want?
Lummus Park Beach on day one set the mood for the whole week. Warm water, cold drinks, great company.
I've done a lot of hikes, but Banff and Jasper are something else. Steve and Kate were the best.
The canyons were incredible. The desert gets really hot in the afternoon, so bring a big water bottle.
Beautiful skies every single night. Some of the drives were long, so bring a good playlist.
Ben knew exactly where to stand for the best view. We saw the lights twice and both times were unreal.
Three days was just right. Cozy days, glowing nights and the friendliest guides.
The views were nice, but I learned I don't really like wine. Five days of tastings was way too many for me.
I've never seen colors like the walls of Antelope Canyon. Ten days went by way too fast.
Easy walks, big views and lovely people. I came home calmer than I left.
Jumping out of a plane over San Diego: done! The pace is wild, so only book this if you love being busy.
